findings.description: Directly inspected all five current views and six poses after redistributing the shorts wrap boundary from 160 mm transverse by 240 mm longitudinal to 200 mm by 207.846 mm. The crouch still shows a bright triangular discontinuity and the sit retains a pale inter-thigh sheet. Width redistribution alone did not resolve the pose appearance; the four matched 0.144222 m seams remain the construction constraint. No fit, opacity, strain, Shape Key or runtime acceptance. Current weighted-mesh distance measurement: wrap median distance to the deformed avatar is 3.6 mm neutral, 34.3 mm crouched, and 44.8 mm seated. Mean wrap thigh weight is 0.092 with 0.908 Hips weight; adjacent front-panel mean thigh weight is 0.267. Controlled same-side thigh-follow and neutral rest-surface-follow candidates did not materially improve directly inspected crouch/sit coverage. Nearest-body-triangle weight transfer on the four shorts panels materially worsened the seated render: median thigh weights increased from 0.267–0.284 to 0.899–0.920, with exposed body and collapsed fabric; experiment evidence: .image2outfit/products/siroino-lilac-lame-fencing-practice-set/experiment-shorts-panel-body-weight-transfer.json. All 156 shared sewn-boundary vertices and all weights outside the four panel interiors remained unchanged. A six-pose target-body trajectory weight fit also failed visual review: the four-panel interiors changed while all 156 shared seam vertices and all outside vertices remained unchanged; median body-surface trajectory residual moved only from 1.013 mm to 1.008 mm and p95 from 148.1 mm to 61.0 mm, yet direct crouch/sit renders show new exposure/collapse while the pale sheet remains. The nearest-body trajectory objective does not encode garment ease or coverage; its residual is not a fit score. Constant weight offsets, neutral surface projection, direct body-weight transfer, and body-surface trajectory fitting have not resolved the pose defect. No fit or appearance acceptance. Canonical sewn-edge audit: the wrap shares 16 vertex IDs with each of the four shorts panels, and maximum absolute Hips/UpperLeg_L/UpperLeg_R weight delta is 0 at every matched edge vertex. Across the 60 unique shared boundary vertices, mean Hips/thigh weights are 0.961/0.039; across the 230 interior vertices they are 0.894/0.106. The low thigh influence is therefore localized to the panel interior; sewn-edge weights already match.

Directly inspected all five refreshed views and six poses. The standing skirt remains a broad A-line with irregular folds rather than clearly ordered pleats. Crouch, sit and prone show large angular rear/between-leg sheets and curled or collapsed hem sections. No appearance or cloth-motion acceptance.

Directly inspected all five refreshed views and six poses. Sleeve and underarm transitions remain visibly faceted and wrinkled in neutral, raised-arm and crossed-arm views; the collar still reads as a tall open cylindrical rim. The diagonal lilac closure reads as a broad strip, while narrow edging and rear waist tab remain hard to distinguish. Surface, neckline, measured fit, strain, clearance and runtime remain unverified.
Upper front torso overlap remains visible and front edges remain unfastened. Sewn waistband now covers the former neutral waist transition gap, but jacket retention and waist fit are not accepted.

Outer shoulder edge now uses an evaluated body surface support sample rather than the UpperArm bone height. Tall collar persists. Head clearance, collar strain and continuous surface intersection remain unapproved; historical seam lengths are bound to their original source hashes.

Current eleven images inspected: sleeve folds remain visible, especially underarm/rear and arms-up. Earlier cuff/clearance measurements and their improvements are historical, bound to prior source hashes; they are not current-source measured fit evidence. Continuous clearance, strain, Large and runtime remain unverified.

All five current views and six poses directly inspected after 140 mm skirt length, reference-ratio flare, matching flat pattern intake and current-input native bending solve. Standing flare is improved over the previous narrow skirt. Irregular folds, front sag/dent and insufficient visible under-shorts remain; broad ordered reference pleats are not achieved. No final appearance acceptance.

Current crouch and sit directly inspected: front skirt forms raised broad flaps, side/rear hem curls and shorts coverage remains unaccepted. Prone also inspected. Skirt transfer to thigh bones is a hypothesis to investigate using actual current vertex weights; no continuous penetration, dynamic cloth, strain or runtime acceptance is claimed.

Current arms-up and arm-cross directly inspected: underarm/sleeve folds persist; collar remains tall. Waist appears assembled in the rendered pose but measured fit, strain and continuous clearance remain unverified.
